stage1.impression: A dark, muddy-orange street at night where the shopfront takes up a quarter of the frame and is outshone by a street-lamp hotspot on the neighbour's blank wall. The window glow, the café curtains and the sconces are a nice idea, but the facades are flat untextured CG plaster, the door is a black hole, the name on the glass reads as dim greenish blocks, and no product or colour shows through the glass. It reads as an architectural massing render, not a photograph.

blocking_9: The shopfront fills at least half the frame width and is clearly the brightest, warmest thing in it (window median lum above the neighbour facades')
The gold-leaf name reads as gold and is legible from the street (delta E 2000 under 15 against a gold reference)
The facades, pavement and street carry real material detail (plaster or stucco grain, kerb wear, wet-asphalt texture) with no flat uniform panels
Cool exterior light against the warm interior, with real blue in the shadows instead of the single orange cast across the frame
Something alive or coloured reads through the glass (an Ember speaker's red, or guests in silhouette), so the room reads as a listening bar and not an empty box
The recessed door and the transom read as lit architecture, not crushed black

defects.what: Street-lamp hotspot on the right-hand neighbour's flat wall (p95 lum 126) is the brightest area in the frame and pulls the eye off the shop
Neighbour's window is one perfectly flat glowing panel (lum range 1.0): reads as a placeholder
Left facade is flat and untextured, with crushed black windows
Bay window glass is flat grey (lum range 14.7) with no reflections, nothing behind it, no frame detail
Gold-leaf name reads as dim olive-green blocks against the backlight; the striped E looks like aliasing or missing geometry
Recessed door is 92% crushed to black
Transom is described as lit but sits at median lum 15 with 29% crush
Window interior has no blue at all (b median 0): one orange cast, no colour separation; the room reads empty, with no speakers, people or props visible
Pavement and kerb are a flat untextured slab with a hard CG edge
Wet street reflects the window only faintly; the bright reflection at bottom right belongs to the neighbour's lamp, not the shop

changes.problem: The shopfront is small and off to one side, so the frame is mostly the neighbours' blank walls.

evidence.measured: Shopfront spans about x 295-800 of 1200 (42%) including the dark upper floor; the lit window is only x 345-660 (26%).

change.to: position [-8.5, 6.0, 1.45], 50 mm, at [0.0, 3.2, 1.9]; shift up so the transom and fascia sit in the top third and the wet street in the bottom fifth

changes.expected: The lit window and door fill about 55-60% of the frame width, the line of sight runs further into the room (towards the listening room's Ember pair), the neighbours shrink to the edges, and there is room for type on the upper facade.

changes.problem: The room's glow is too weak to be the hero; the whole frame is underexposed.

evidence.measured: Frame median lum 17.9, 85.3% of pixels below 40; window median 19.5 against the right facade's 57.1.

change.to: sconces 25 W, pendants 90 W, exposure 0.9 (keep the street lamps as set in c3 so the ratio favours the interior)

changes.expected: The window glows at a median lum of about 55-75 with highlights near 200 on the shades and no clipping beyond the bulbs; the frame median rises to about 30.

changes.problem: A street lamp floods the neighbour's wall and becomes the brightest, most saturated area in the frame.

evidence.measured: Median lum 57.1, p95 125.9; x-profile peaks at 105.5, twice the shop window's p95 of 57.

change.to: 2 x point, 90 W, 4000 K (cool LED, as on SF streets), moved so neither falls on a facade at less than 3 m; one placed behind the camera at left to rake the pavement and the wet street

changes.expected: The neighbour walls fall to a median lum of about 20-30, cool grey; the brightest area becomes the shop window; cool light on the street sets off the warm interior.

changes.problem: The gold-leaf name reads as dim olive-green blocks, not gold.

evidence.measured: Mean RGB (62,42,11), delta E 2000 of 47.5 against gold #C9A24A; the backlit leaf is a silhouette.

change.setting: the gold leaf (emission) plus a new exterior lamp
change.to: emission 0.4, metallic gold with roughness 0.25, and one small warm spot (2700 K, 15 W, cone 25 deg) under the fascia aimed at the lettering from outside, so the leaf picks up a specular glint; check the E's geometry (it shows stripes)

changes.expected: The name reads at a glance as bright gold leaf with a gilded edge, lum about 120-170.

changes.problem: One orange cast covers everything; there is no blue anywhere, so there is no warm-against-cool night contrast.

evidence.measured: Window b_median 0; left facade b_median 0; even the street b_median 1.

change.to: white_balance_k 3200 with a dusk-blue sky dome (about 9000 K, strength 0.05) so the shadows and the upper floors go blue-grey

changes.expected: The facades and street sit in cool blue-grey (b_median above r_median in the shadows), and the interior stays amber and reads warmer by contrast.

changes.problem: The facades, the neighbour's window and the pavement are flat, untextured CG surfaces.

evidence.measured: Neighbour window lum range 1.0 (a uniform panel); facades show no grain or variation; the kerb is a plain slab.

change.from: flat plaster, flat panel, plain pavement
change.to: painted stucco with fine grain and roughness variation, painted window trim, real glass on the neighbour's window with a dim dressed interior or a pulled blind, concrete pavement with joints and wear, wet asphalt with puddles and roughness 0.05-0.4

changes.expected: Every surface holds micro-detail at full size, and the neighbour window shows a lum range above 20 with reflections.

changes.problem: The recessed door and the transom, which the frame is meant to show lit, are crushed.

evidence.measured: Door 91.5% crushed, median 0; transom x 300-800 y 280-340 median 15, crush 29%.

change.setting: a new lamp at the door plus the transom glow
change.from: no light in the recess; transom lit only by spill
change.to: a small warm downlight in the door recess (2400 K, 12 W) and a glass door that shows the room; transom backlit by a soffit strip at 2.0

changes.expected: The door reads as an inviting lit recess at median lum about 25-40, and the transom glows as a band at about 45.

changes.problem: The room reads empty through the glass: no guests, no props in view, none of the speakers' colour.

evidence.measured: The interior shows only curtains, sconces and the lettering; no red reads anywhere (the window's r/g ratio is the even orange of the sconces).

change.to: two or three guests in soft silhouette above the café curtains at the window counter, glasses and a candle on the sill, and a light haze in the room at 0.02 per metre so the sconce beams read

changes.expected: The room reads as a lived-in bar at a glance; haze gives depth behind the glass.

out_of_scope.request: Make an Ember speaker visible through the window (for example nearer the glass)
out_of_scope.why: That changes the room's layout, which is fixed; the camera change c1 should try to frame the existing Ember pair down the room's depth instead.
